name: First Rate Metal Fab
old_description: When you require excellent metal fabrication services, turn to First Rate Metal Fab in Manor, PA. We have a solid reputation in the industry because of our fast turnaround time and the exceptional work we deliver. If you entrust your fabrication needs to us, expect that we will provide you with products that are second to none.
about:
First Rate Metal Fab, based in Manor, Pennsylvania, was founded in 2009 as a family-owned and operated business. The company was established to address the need for outstanding metal fabrication services, combining decades of hands-on experience with modern equipment.

The shop specializes in precision sheet metal fabrication, offering design assistance, prototyping, short and long production runs, punching, bending, hardware insertion, welding, laser cutting, shearing, powder coating, assembly, and inspection. Equipment includes an Amada Vipros 345 punch press, Amada press brakes, a Bodor 3 kW fiber laser, an Amada Plusar laser, an Accu Shear, Haeger insertion presses, a Timesaver 137 surface finisher, and multiple welding systems. The facility handles materials such as stainless steel, aluminum, copper, carbon steel, and brass.

First Rate Metal Fab serves original equipment manufacturers and other businesses in the electronics, communications, and transportation industries. The company also provides local delivery throughout western and central Pennsylvania, including Erie, Greensburg, Pittsburgh, State College, and Uniontown.

The company emphasizes honesty and integrity as guiding values, quick turnaround times, proactive communication with progress updates, and a reliable, experienced team. It positions itself as a partner that treats customers like family, willing to take on prototype and short-run work while also supporting large-volume production.

name: Fisher Textiles
old_description: Fisher Textiles has supplied engineered fabrics for digital textile printing since 1988. Our award-winning knit and woven fabrics support dye sublimation, UV, Latex, and solvent printing for applications ranging from trade shows to retail lightboxes, with widths up to 197 inches.
about:
Fisher Textiles, based in Matthews, North Carolina, has supplied engineered fabrics for digital textile printing since 1988. Founded as a textile converting operation, the company pivoted in the mid-1990s to develop polyester fabrics specifically for wide-format dye sublimation, establishing itself in the emerging soft signage market. In 2023, a strategic investment from American Pacific Group (APG) brought new capital and made Fisher Textiles a sister company to digital print production partner Media One.

The company produces knit and woven fabrics compatible with dye sublimation, direct dye sublimation, UV, latex, pigment, and solvent ink systems, with widths up to 197 inches. Its 82,000-square-foot headquarters, opened in 2019, houses expanded warehousing, a print demonstration room, and training space. Nine distribution centers across the U.S. and Canada — including locations in California, Nevada, Texas, Florida, Wisconsin, South Carolina, and Ontario — stock popular products for faster delivery.

Fisher Textiles serves the trade show exhibit, SEG display, retail graphics, backlit signage, banner, home furnishings, gaming table, and performance apparel markets. Its recycled-fabric line uses post-consumer PET bottles, and a take-back program repurposes used signage into new fiber-based products.

The company emphasizes quality consistency, technical expertise, fast response, reliable inventory, and long-term customer partnerships — values maintained from its early days in a 3,000-square-foot leased facility to its current national footprint.

name: Flatbed Firewood and Lumber
old_description: Maybe you can’t find an activity all your friends will agree on, or maybe you need a way to pass the time at your next event. about:
Flatbed Firewood and Lumber operates from Bismarck, North Dakota, where it was founded in 2010. The company began as a firewood supplier and has since expanded into mobile entertainment, lumber processing, and equipment distribution.

The business runs three main lines: a mobile axe-throwing trailer that travels to events across the region; a firewood operation supplying restaurants and residents; and a wood shop producing live-edge slabs and custom stair treads milled from hardwood and softwood trees harvested locally. It also serves as an authorized dealer for Prime Attachments, stocking backhoes, earth augers, pallet forks, and other skid-steer implements.

Customers include event planners seeking on-site entertainment, Bismarck-area restaurants buying cooking wood, custom home builders incorporating one-of-a-kind stair treads and slabs into Parade of Homes projects, and contractors needing skid-steer attachments. The company notes that its stair treads have been featured in multiple Bismarck Parade of Homes showcases.

Flatbed Firewood emphasizes sustainable sourcing, reclaiming urban trees from North Dakota boulevards for its stair treads and slabs. The mobile axe-throwing trailer is promoted as a turnkey party solution, while the Prime Attachments dealership provides immediate access to a full line of skid-steer tools.

about:
Fluorolite Plastics LLC operates from Hudson, Massachusetts. The company is a woman-owned business that states it has been for over 45 years, specializing in replacement light covers for fluorescent and LED fixtures.

The firm manufactures a wide range of plastic and glass light diffusers, including flat sheets, wrap-around lenses, tube guards, vapor-tight fixtures, parabolic louvers, and egg-crate panels. It offers acrylic sheets in clear, transparent, or solid colors and uses a laser cutter to produce custom sizes and shapes. For non-stock profiles, the shop custom molds and vacuum forms thousands of different replacement covers for both commercial and residential projects.

Fluorolite serves commercial contractors, municipal street-lighting departments, and residential customers. Examples cited include kitchen under-cabinet diffusers, decorative cloud panels, and street-light refractors. The company also supports large-scale commercial projects and provides free quotes via an online form or email.

The company emphasizes its long-standing service record, competitive pricing, and award-winning support team, highlighted by Best of Framingham awards in 2021 and 2022. Its differentiators include in-house custom molding, vacuum forming, and laser cutting, allowing rapid turnaround on bespoke parts.

name: Forsey's Fine Furniture and Interior Design
old_description: Forsey’s has been dedicated to quality, craftsmanship and exceptional customer service. Founded by brothers Jack and Harry Forsey, their vision for providing the finest home furnishings and interior design has carried on for over 74 years and is now in its 3rd generation of family ownership.
about:
Forsey's Fine Furniture and Interior Design has operated from Salt Lake City, Utah, since 1951, when brothers Jack and Harry Forsey founded the business on a model specializing in American-made Colonial Maple home furnishings. The company remains in its third generation of family ownership, now led by Jack Forsey and his wife Michelle.

The retailer carries over 40 brands of home furnishings, the vast majority manufactured in the United States, Canada, or Europe, and operates two showrooms on Highland Drive — one dedicated exclusively to Stickley Furniture, for which Forsey's has been the exclusive Utah dealer since the late 1990s, and a second multi-vendor showroom. Beyond retail sales, the company provides interior design services, free in-home consultations, commercial project furnishing, and drop-ship delivery across the continental United States, supported by a white-glove delivery team.

Customers range from residential buyers seeking a single piece to designers and businesses outfitting large commercial spaces. The company's vendor relationships emphasize domestically and ethically sourced products, and its staff — composed of designers, artists, and other professionals — works without commission to focus on client needs.

Forsey's differentiates itself through a pressure-free, family-owned culture that eliminated commission pay, a curated selection vetted by its design and delivery teams, and a commitment to quality without compromise that has sustained the business for over seven decades.

name: Foster Electric Company, Inc.
old_description: Foster Electric was founded in 1956 by Mr. Aubrey E. Foster, Sr. (1919-2008). At that time, he was the sole employee; and the business was located in the garage at his residence. Mr. Foster would arise at 4:30 – 5:00 AM each morning and load his vehicle for the day’s deliveries and customer sales. Having completed his rounds by 5:00 – 6:00 PM, he would arrive home to start his office duties: writing up customer orders, invoicing sales, receiving remittances and making deposits, ordering merchandise from manufactures, receiving materials and sorting customer orders for the next day’s business. As you can imagine, his was a very busy schedule. But, in addition to all his business duties, he still found time for his family, church and community commitments.
about:
Foster Electric Company, Inc. was founded in 1956 by Aubrey E. Foster, Sr. in Lynchburg, Virginia. The business began in the garage of Foster's residence, where he operated as the sole employee, handling deliveries, sales, invoicing, and procurement. In 1958 the company moved to a downtown storefront and by 1965 had relocated to a 14,000‑square‑foot facility on Campbell Avenue with seven employees. The current 45,000‑square‑foot office and warehouse complex was acquired in 1982. Today the company is an employee‑owned ESOP led by President Duane White.

From its Lynchburg facility Foster Electric operates as a full‑line electrical supply distributor. The company stocks and sells electrical equipment for residential, commercial, and industrial applications, and provides delivery service throughout central Virginia along with same‑day shipping anywhere in the continental United States. A staff of approximately 32 employees supports sales, warehousing, and logistics operations.

The distributor serves four primary customer segments: residential and small contractors, industrial and commercial large contractors, industrial maintenance/repair/operations (MRO) buyers, and industrial OEM accounts. Its product range covers the needs of construction trades, plant maintenance departments, and original equipment manufacturers across the region.

Foster Electric emphasizes its independence as a locally owned distributor, which it says keeps the company in close contact with customer needs. The firm highlights fast delivery and competitive pricing as core commitments, positioning itself as a value‑added partner rather than a simple reseller.

name: Four Process, LTD
old_description: This drive to be more than just another injection molder is found throughout our woman-owned, third-generation family, small business, from the shop floor to the offices. It’s fueled by four pillars, our 4Ps, on which our company and culture were founded more than 45 years ago:
about:
Four Process, LTD was founded in 1974 in St. Louis, Missouri, by Hubert Fox, a U.S. Army veteran and tool-and-die engineer. The company began as a cast-to-size tooling foundry and machine shop before transitioning to custom precision plastic injection molding. Today it operates as a woman-owned, third-generation family small business headquartered in Valley Park, Missouri.

The company runs a 23,000-square-foot facility equipped with 85- to 500-ton presses, a quality lab, assembly cells, and robotics automation. Its core services include insert molding, over molding, hot-runner and cold-runner injection molding, plus component sourcing, prototyping, part assembly, specialized packaging, sonic welding, adhesive bonding, product testing, and custom inventory management. Four Process handles short-, medium-, and long-run production across a wide range of engineering, commodity, and specialty plastics.

Customers include Rug Doctor and Arundale Products, and the company has produced parts for the shoe, medical-device, and electronics industries. Its cross-trained team supports both transfer work and reshoring projects aimed at reducing supply-chain risk.

Four Process differentiates itself through four cultural pillars—communication, honesty, value, and reliability—and a proactive, data-driven approach that includes custom inventory programs to prevent shortages and accelerate fulfillment.
